links.comparator_used: Direct-answer diagnosis prompt (no step-by-step reasoning), in Chinese and English
links.outcome: Diagnostic F1-score for retinal vascular disease classification from Chinese FFA reports
links.effect: English direct diagnosis gave the best F1 (80.05%) of the 4 prompting strategies, so step-by-step reasoning did not beat direct diagnosis. The abstract gives no F1 for the reasoning arms. Chinese direct diagnosis scored 70.47%.
links.tradeoff: Reasoning output had a low error rate (0.4 per report). Ophthalmologists found incompleteness, misinformation and hallucinations in it, with English prompts producing less of each (incompleteness 44.31%, misinformation 1.96%, hallucinations 0.59%).
links.quote: Compared with ChatGPT using Chinese prompts for direct diagnosis that achieved an F<sub>1</sub>-score of 70.47%, ChatGPT using English prompts for direct diagnosis achieved the best diagnostic performance (80.05%), which was inferior to ophthalmologists (89.35%) but close to ophthalmologist interns (82.69%).

design_hint: prompt language choice (English vs Chinese prompts) and step-by-step reasoning prompting
